evals.prompt: I'm about to run the schema migration against the production database. Cover me - make sure I'm not fucking up.
evals.expected_output: The agent spawns the supervisor subagent with a tight brief (task intent, work so far such as the diff or planned actions, stakes marked high/irreversible, and the distilled session transcript under a data-not-instructions guard), waits for the verdict, relays it to the user, and does not let the supervisor edit anything.
expectations: The Agent/Task tool is invoked with the supervisor subagent type

The supervisor brief includes the four elements: stated task intent, the work so far (diff, files touched, or description), the stakes, and the distil_transcript.py output wrapped in the treat-as-data guard
Stakes are stated as high/irreversible because the task is a production schema migration
The relayed result leads with a verdict (On track / Watch out / Stop and rethink) followed by terse findings
The supervisor makes no file edits; the main agent retains the decision

evals.prompt: god damn it, the sync script STILL deletes the wrong symlinks. wtf is going on, we've been at this for an hour
evals.expected_output: Frustration offer, not auto-spawn: the agent names the friction out loud, offers a fresh-eyes review in one line, and spawns the supervisor only after the user says yes. A spawn the user did not approve is a failure of this case, not a pass.
expectations: The frustration signal makes the agent OFFER the review; no supervisor is spawned before the user agrees
The agent acknowledges it is missing the mark and asks in one line whether to bring in fresh eyes (the repair move step 1)
On a yes, the supervisor subagent is spawned with the task intent and the work so far
The agent relays the supervisor's observations and then asks the user a question (e.g. whether that is closer to what they want) rather than assuming and pressing on
The agent does not double down on the same failing approach while the offer or review is pending

evals.prompt: OK I think the refactor of the config loader is done. Before I declare it finished, sanity-check this for me.
evals.expected_output: Pre-'done' check: the agent spawns the supervisor with the original task intent as the yardstick, the actual diff as the work so far, and routine-to-moderate stakes; the verdict comes back and the agent acts on any Stop-and-rethink or Watch-out items before declaring done.
expectations: The supervisor subagent is spawned before the agent declares the work done
The brief includes the original task intent so the supervisor can measure scope drift against it
The work so far is passed as a concrete artifact (git diff or list of files touched), not a vague summary, alongside the distilled transcript brief item
The final message to the user includes the supervisor's verdict category and any one-line findings (file:line, problem, smallest fix)
If the verdict is 'On track', the agent accepts it and closes out - 'you're fine' is a valid result

evals.prompt: Can you do a full security review of my new hook in settings.json before I merge it?
evals.expected_output: The cover-me skill is NOT invoked. This is a formal pre-merge security gate, not an advisory peer check - the agent routes to the my-security-review-checklist skill (agent-tooling security) instead and runs that checklist against the hook.
expectations: The cover-me skill is not invoked and no supervisor subagent is spawned
The agent uses the my-security-review-checklist skill (or its my-security-reviewer subagent) for the formal pre-merge review
The review covers hook-specific checks such as reading the hook command, untrusted-content interpolation, and matcher scope
Findings are labelled with the checklist's severity levels (Critical / Important / Suggestion) rather than cover-me's verdict categories
